cases.rationale: The board is the writable wall surface. The eraser is an accessory.
The inkjet takes sheets. The thermal printer takes roll stock.
Destroying documents by cutting them into strips identifies the shredder.
The black classic desktop model is distinct from the blue long-arm booklet model.
The booklet stapler has the required reach. The compact desktop stapler does not.
The two heads remove material. Neither stapler makes holes intended for binder rings.
Of the listed devices, the standalone calculator performs arithmetic.
The catalog has one optical barcode reader.
Thermal receipts come from roll stock. The inkjet takes sheets.
The requested tool clears the board. The board itself is the surface.
Both the sheet-fed inkjet and the receipt printer satisfy the stated request.
The exact broken unit must be replaced. Both stapler models are plausible and the order supplies no identifying detail.
No projector exists in this frozen catalog. A whiteboard cannot project slides.
No listed printer has evidence of waterproof certification. Model fabrication or certification claims are out of scope.
